newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TAIWAN BUYS 750,000/BBL SEPT REFORMATE AT $24.19/B.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN BUYS 750,000/BBL SEPT REFORMATE AT $24.19/B.

text.p: After long-drawn negotiations, Taiwan state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought by tender 750,000 barrels of September reformate at $24.19 per barrel, cost-and-freight (c-and-f), a CPC official said on Wednesday.
CPC bought the three 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane unleaded reformate from different sellers.
"They were all awarded at the same price...from different sellers," he said.

He denied earlier rumours of of purchases from a U.S. major at $24.20 for September 1-15 delivery, another from a Japanese trader at $24.35 for September 16-30 and the third from another U.S. major at $24.25.
Although the tender closed August 11 and was valid for two days, CPC spent longer than the usual one day to it takes to deliberate the offers.

After the close of the tender, CPC officials told Reuters it had received nine offers over $24.00 per barrel in its 95-octane unleaded reformate import tender for September, and would try to counter offer at $24.10 or $24.20.
The official said no further September tenders will be issued as the award was "enough for the month."
It took the large volume after it cancelled an earlier tender for the deliveries for first half of September due to high offers over $25.30.
Taiwan usually buys one to two cargoes every half-month.
In August, CPC bought three cargoes, two for Aug 1-10 delivery at around $24.60-$24.76 and one for Aug 11-20 at $23.30, c-and-f Taiwan.
